title: [Bugs] SMF does not release the CHF charging session when PDU session create fails at ApplySessionRules
body:
## Bug Description

To set up a PDU session, the SMF opens a charging session on the CHF: `CreateChargingSession` sends `CHARGING_INIT` and remembers the returned charging reference (`smContext.ChargingDataRef`). If the session setup then fails, the SMF should close that charging session again with `CHARGING_RELEASE`. The setup failure path does not do that.

Right after opening the charging session, the create applies the PCF's session rules (`ApplySessionRules`). If that fails, the handler calls `makeEstRejectResAndReleaseSMContext`, which runs the SMF's cleanup, `RemoveSMContextFromAllNF`. That cleanup terminates the SM policy on the PCF, unsubscribes from the UDM and removes the SMContext. It has no charging release at all. `ReleaseChargingSession` (`CHARGING_RELEASE`) is only called from the normal PDU session release handlers.

So the SMF rejects the session, cleans up everything else, and leaves the charging session open on the CHF. It has also just deleted the SMContext that held the only copy of `ChargingDataRef`, so nothing in the SMF can ever close it later. Every such failed setup leaves one more open charging session on the CHF.

### The create opens the charging session first.

https://github.com/free5gc/smf/blob/2232d2992f204207e58830ac8ee55bf0cd832f92/internal/sbi/processor/pdu_session.go#L249-L252

`HandlePDUSessionSMContextCreate` selects a CHF and calls `CreateChargingSession` (`:252`). `CreateChargingSession` sends `CHARGING_INIT` and stores the reference the CHF returns in `smContext.ChargingDataRef`.

```go
if err = p.Consumer().CHFSelection(smContext); err != nil {
	logger.PduSessLog.Errorln("chf selection error:", err)
} else {
	p.CreateChargingSession(smContext)                                   // :252  CHARGING_INIT to the CHF
}
```

### The next step can fail, and its failure exit goes to the cleanup.

https://github.com/free5gc/smf/blob/2232d2992f204207e58830ac8ee55bf0cd832f92/internal/sbi/processor/pdu_session.go#L255-L262

`ApplySessionRules` (`:256`) installs the session rules from the PCF's SM policy decision. It returns an error when the context ends up with no session rule (`sm_context_policy.go:44-46`). The handler then calls `makeEstRejectResAndReleaseSMContext` and returns.

```go
if err = smContext.ApplySessionRules(smPolicyDecision); err != nil {    // :256
	smContext.Log.Errorf("PDUSessionSMContextCreate err: %v", err)
	p.makeEstRejectResAndReleaseSMContext(c, smContext,
		nasMessage.Cause5GSMRequestRejectedUnspecified,
		&smf_errors.SubscriptionDenied)                                  // -> RemoveSMContextFromAllNF
	return
}
```

### The cleanup releases the SM policy, but not the charging session.

https://github.com/free5gc/smf/blob/2232d2992f204207e58830ac8ee55bf0cd832f92/internal/sbi/processor/sm_common.go#L7-L49

`RemoveSMContextFromAllNF()` terminates the SM policy on the PCF when `smContext.SMPolicyID != ""` (`:17`), unsubscribes from the UDM, and then removes the SMContext (`:49`). There is no `ReleaseChargingSession` call in it, and nothing checks `smContext.ChargingDataRef`.

```go
func (p *Processor) RemoveSMContextFromAllNF(smContext *smf_context.SMContext, sendNotification bool) {
	smContext.SetState(smf_context.InActive)
	// ...
	if smContext.SMPolicyID != "" {
		if err := p.Consumer().SendSMPolicyAssociationTermination(smContext); err != nil {   // :17  SM policy DELETE to the PCF
			smContext.Log.Errorf("SM Policy Termination failed: %s", err)
		} else {
			smContext.SMPolicyID = ""
		}
	}
	// ... UDM unsubscribe ...
	// <-- no ReleaseChargingSession / CHARGING_RELEASE
	go p.sendSMContextStatusNotificationAndRemoveSMContext(smContext, sendNotification)       // -> RemoveSMContext(ref) at :49
}
```

### The charging release exists, but only on the normal release paths.

https://github.com/free5gc/smf/blob/2232d2992f204207e58830ac8ee55bf0cd832f92/internal/sbi/processor/charging_trigger.go#L64-L68

`ReleaseChargingSession` sends `CHARGING_RELEASE`. It is called from `HandlePDUSessionSMContextRelease` and `HandlePDUSessionSMContextLocalRelease` on `SessionReleaseSuccess`. The create failure path never calls it.

```go
func (p *Processor) ReleaseChargingSession(smContext *smf_context.SMContext) {
	// ...
	p.Consumer().SendConvergedChargingRequest(smContext, smf_context.CHARGING_RELEASE, multipleUnitUsage)
```

**What makes the create fail here.** `ApplySessionRules` fails whenever the SM policy decision from the PCF leaves the context with no session rule. The charging session has already been opened at that point, so any such failure leaves it open.

## To Reproduce

On SMF v1.4.3, driven through the project's own SMF unit-test harness (`internal/sbi/processor/pdu_session_test.go`): gock-stubbed NRF/UDM/PCF/CHF and a stub PFCP, no real UPF. **No change to the SMF source.** The only harness change is the PFCP listen address.

**How charging is opened.** The NRF stub lets the SMF discover a CHF, so `CHFSelection` succeeds and `CreateChargingSession` sends `CHARGING_INIT`. The CHF stub answers with `201` and a charging reference.

**How the create is made to fail.** The PCF stub answers `POST /sm-policies` with `201` and an SM policy decision whose `sessRules` is empty. `ApplySessionRules` then returns `"ApplySessionRules: no session rule"`, and the handler takes the `:256` failure exit into `makeEstRejectResAndReleaseSMContext`. This is the natural failure path, with no injection.

**What is sent.** 30 `POST /nsmf-pdusession/v1/sm-contexts`, one per UE: 30 distinct SUPIs, each with PDU Session ID 10.

**What is counted.** The stubs count requests with `gock.Observe`:
- `CHARGING_INIT` reaching the CHF (`POST .../chargingdata`)
- `CHARGING_RELEASE` reaching the CHF (`POST .../chargingdata/{ref}/release`)
- SM policy terminations reaching the PCF (`POST .../sm-policies/{id}/delete`)

The SM policy terminations show that the cleanup actually ran. On the SMF, the test also checks the SMContext pool with `GetSMContextById(supi, pduSessionId)`.

```
                       HTTP | CHARGING_INIT sent | CHARGING_RELEASE sent | SM policy terminations sent
  after 1 UE            403 |                  1 |                     0 |                           1
  after 10 UEs          403 |                 10 |                     0 |                          10
  after 30 UEs          403 |                 30 |                     0 |                          30

total: 30 UEs, 30 charging sessions opened on the CHF, 0 released; 30 SM policies terminated, 30 SMContexts removed
```

**The leak.**
- All 30 creates open a charging session on the CHF and then fail at `ApplySessionRules`.
- The cleanup runs every time. The PCF receives all 30 SM policy terminations, and all 30 SMContexts are removed from the SMF pool (0 left at the end).
- But not one `CHARGING_RELEASE` reaches the CHF.
- The cleanup that runs on this path simply has no charging release, so each failed create leaves one open charging session on the CHF.

**The accumulation.** The count of open charging sessions rises by exactly one per failed create. The SMContext that held `ChargingDataRef` has been removed, so the SMF has no record left to release it with, and no later procedure in the SMF revisits it. The open sessions stay on the CHF until the CHF expires them by its own means.

## Expected Behavior

When a PDU session create fails after CHARGING_INIT has been sent to the CHF, the SMF should send CHARGING_RELEASE for that charging session before discarding the SMContext, so that no charging session is left open on the CHF.

## Trace Files

### Configuration Files

N/A. The PoC runs under the project's `pdu_session_test.go` harness with gock-stubbed NRF/UDM/PCF/CHF and a stub PFCP; reproduction conditions are described above.

### PCAP File

N/A. This is a code-logic issue, unrelated to the packet level.

### Log File

One failed create:

```
[INFO][SMF][PduSess] CHF Selection for SMContext SUPI[imsi-208930000030000] PDUSessionID[10]
[INFO][SMF][Charging] Handle SendConvergedChargingRequest
[INFO][SMF][Charging] Send Charging Data Request[Init] successfully
[ERRO][SMF][PduSess][pdu_session_id:10][supi:imsi-208930000030000] PDUSessionSMContextCreate err: ApplySessionRules: no session rule
[INFO][SMF][PduSess] UE[imsi-208930000030000] PDUSessionID[10] Release IP[10.60.0.1]
[INFO][SMF][PduSess][pdu_session_id:10][supi:imsi-208930000030000] smContext[urn:uuid:ecb02e76-f93d-4f7f-b114-f87fb377ecd9] is deleted from pool
```

The init is sent and the SMContext is deleted from the pool, but no charging release is logged. Over the whole run, `ApplySessionRules: no session rule` and `is deleted from pool` each appear 30 times.

## Additional Context

Every create that opens a charging session and then fails at `ApplySessionRules` leaves one open charging session on the CHF. The SMF has already sent a reject, so neither the AMF nor the UE will ever release this session. The SMF itself has deleted the SMContext and with it `ChargingDataRef`, so it cannot release it either.

This is a different bug from the SM policy leak on the async reject path. There, the whole cleanup is skipped. Here, the cleanup runs to completion and only the charging release is missing from it, so the SM policy is terminated correctly while the charging session is not.

## How did we find?

We found this bug by using our (work-in-progress) static analysis tool, manually verified it, and made a runnable PoC.
